extracted.intended_audience: government attorneys, military department legal officers, and officials responsible for administration of federal public lands and military reservations
extracted.subtask_description: Legal and administrative standards governing title, possession, jurisdiction, use, removal of trespassers, and disposition of property and improvements on United States public and military reservations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deed recital of statutory compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The deed should preferably contain recitals showing that the provisions of the act of Congress under which it was given were complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit recitals in conveyances to the United States evidencing compliance with the enabling statute to avoid defects or disputes about authority under which the land was conveyed.

rubrics_metrics.name: United States not subject to adverse possession
rubrics_metrics.description: While the United States is entitled to avail itself of statutes of limitation, it is not bound thereby; occupancy by private parties, however long continued, gives them no title thereto as against the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat long user or possession as creating title against the sovereign; claims of prescriptive title or adverse possession against the United States are generally without legal foundation.

rubrics_metrics.name: No title by continued use through military reservation
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim of a right of way for a road through a military reservation based on continued use does not create title by user since the reservation was purchased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assert that use alone cannot give parties title or rights over land already reserved or purchased for military use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescriptive title against sovereign invalid
rubrics_metrics.description: Prescriptive claims (e.g., to water power) based on long possession, even if accompanied by claim of title, are without legal foundation against the sovereign under common and civil law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenge prescriptive assertions against federal ownership; cite precedent refusing to recognize such titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injunction protects US title and possession against continuous trespass
rubrics_metrics.description: Where title and possession of the United States to land (e.g., cemetery) have been duly purchased, they may be protected by injunction against continuous municipal trespass because damages are inadequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek injunctive relief when continuous physical interference threatens federal property and monetary damages would be inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for removing unlawful occupants
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons who have entered unlawfully upon a military reservation and cultivated soil or diverted water should be given reasonable notice to quit with their property, and if they do not comply, may be removed by military force beyond the limits of the reservation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commandants should give reasonable notice before forcible removal; removal may proceed if occupants refuse to leave after notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal officers must respect judicial process
rubrics_metrics.description: A United States officer or agent in charge of lands sued in court should appear and answer; he is not authorized to interpose physical force against service of due process even if he believes the suit groundless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not obstruct judicial process with military force; withdraw protective force or ensure it does not obstruct execution of judicial process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title to streets/highways with lot purchases
rubrics_metrics.description: Purchase of land bounded by streets or highways gives title to the center of the street where such title is in the grantor unless conveyance excludes the street; upon vacation of streets within a reservation the unencumbered title is in the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine conveyance language for exclusion of streets; where streets effectively lead into reservation or are abandoned, title may vest in the United States or result in a private easement appurtenant for ingress/egress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Easement/appurtenant rights acquired with lot purchases
rubrics_metrics.description: If title to streets did not pass with lots, the Government by purchase of several lots may acquire appurtenant private easement or servitude for egress and ingress to the lots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where conveyances are ambiguous, consider that purchase of multiple lots may confer easement rights rather than fee title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conveyances to sea and water boundary rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A deed describing land as extending to 'the sea' or 'along the sea' will convey only to high-water mark unless the deed specifically includes low-water mark or state law gives private title to low-water mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft deeds to the United States to expressly include low-water mark and adequate water-covered lands where necessary for fortifications or other federal uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bed and shore ownership between State and US
rubrics_metrics.description: As between the United States and a State, the soil of the bed of navigable waters and shores below high-water mark (or ordinary water line on non-tidal rivers) belongs to the State; natural accretions to private land belong to the private owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize State title to tidelands; federal interest in submerged lands exists only where ceded by the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvements erected by US on State land
rubrics_metrics.description: A granite monument erected by the United States under congressional appropriation on State land became the property of that State as a fixed improvement in absence of statute or agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appropriations fund improvements on non-federal land, secure statutory or contractual provisions governing ownership and disposition of the improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Buildings erected jure belli in enemy territory
rubrics_metrics.description: Buildings erected by the United States on land occupied jure belli in an enemy's country are not governed by the rule that improvements become landowner's property; on surrender the military authorities may legally remove and retain or dispose of the buildings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat temporary wartime improvements differently from ordinary fixtures; document authority for removal or disposal when returning land to owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary vs permanent military structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporary buildings erected by military orders on United States land for temporary purposes are generally personal property of the United States removable by the Secretary of War; permanent structures that are real estate require congressional authority for removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify buildings by permanence to determine removal authority; obtain Congress authorization for disposal of permanent real estate structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized personal use of US land by officers
rubrics_metrics.description: A post commander who, without authority, took possession of United States land to erect a building for personal use and assumed to hold and dispose of it as his own acquired no legal estate; the same applies to permitting enlisted men to erect dwellings as private property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent unauthorized appropriation of federal land by officers or enlisted personnel; ensure such acts are recognized as unauthorized and invalid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of condemnation under purchase contract reserving improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Under a contract for purchase of land reserving improvements, when a small portion is condemned and cost deducted from contract price, condemnation proceedings may give the Government legal title to buildings while equitable title remains in the other contracting party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When negotiating purchase contracts that reserve improvements, address rights and compensation in condemnation scenarios; equitable interests may persist against legal title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timber and wood on military reservations
rubrics_metrics.description: Wood growing on a military reservation is the property of the United States; a contractor who cuts such wood under contract with the United States may not remove or otherwise treat it as his own property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control cutting and removal of timber via proper orders; contractors have rights only as authorized by contract, not independent ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable cutting for fuel permitted despite protection statutes
rubrics_metrics.description: The act to protect ornamental and other trees on Government reservations was not intended to preclude reasonable cutting of wood on military reservations, under direction of the proper officer, for supplying necessary fuel for garrisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow necessary and directed fuel-wood cutting under authority; ensure direction from proper officer to avoid penal liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of reservation
rubrics_metrics.description: A reservation may be defined as a portion of the public lands of the United States withdrawn from the operation of the land laws and set apart by Congress or by the President under authority of law for some administrative purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat reserved lands as distinct from public domain subject to land laws; authority to reserve originates from Congress or the President acting under implied/express authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: State civil process and reservations
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere establishing of a military reservation cannot affect the power of State or Territorial authorities to serve civil or criminal process therein, except insofar as such service is specially precluded or restricted by law or cession of exclusive jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume reservation creates a jurisdictional bar to state process unless explicit cession or statutory restriction exists; review terms of cession for limits on state authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive reservations inoperative as to privately owned land
rubrics_metrics.description: An order reserving lands for public purposes is inoperative as to lands which at the time of issue were not public lands; an executive reservation is void and inoperative as to lands in lawful private ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm public status of lands before relying on an executive reservation; avoid attempting to reserve privately owned parcels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction transfer when setting apart wood reservations
rubrics_metrics.description: When lands within the exterior limits of a military reservation are set apart by the President as a wood reservation for a military post, those lands pass under the jurisdiction of the War Department and cease to be under Interior Department jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate departmental jurisdictional changes when the Executive sets apart subparts of reservations for specific purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on congressional and presidential authority over reservations
rubrics_metrics.description: The President's power in creating military reservations is limited to setting apart and declaring them; the President may add to or modify boundaries by redeclaration but cannot unreserve duly reserved lands absent authority from Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain congressional authorization for any relinquishment or restoration of reserved lands; use redeclaration for boundary adjustments but not for unreserving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to courts when title claims conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Where conflicting claims to title within a reservation are not clearly groundless, the Secretary should not attempt to pass upon the questions but should refer the parties to the courts for legal remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid departmental adjudication of complex title disputes; preserve defenses and refer to judicial process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of lands useless for military purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the act of July 5, 1884, the Secretary of War may place lands which have become useless for military purposes under control of the Secretary of the Interior for disposition and sale as authorized by the statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow statutory process for declaring lands 'useless' and turning them over to Interior; observe existing contracts (e.g., for wood) and defer transfer until performance if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on municipal grants from abandoned reservations
rubrics_metrics.description: The President's power under the act of March 3, 1893 to withhold from sale and grant portions of abandoned military reservations to municipal corporations extends only to reservations turned over to the Secretary of the Interior under the act of July 5, 1884.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the reservation has been properly transferred to Interior under the 1884 act before relying on the 1893 municipal grant authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceeds of sale and allowable expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Section governing disposition of 'old material, condemned stores, supplies, or other public property' requires 'net proceeds' only to be deposited in the Treasury; proper expenses connected with appraisement and sale may be defrayed out of the sum realized from the sale of a military reservation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for reasonable sale-related expenses against gross proceeds before depositing net into Treasury; document costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reservations in territories and ceded possessions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under treaties and statutes (e.g., with Spain), ownership of public buildings and lands in ceded territories passed to the United States; the President was authorized to make reservations of public lands in such territories within specified timeframes, after which unreserved public lands passed to local governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act promptly to have required reservations made in newly acquired territories to preserve federal control as authorized by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mineral entry rights not applicable to reservations
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory rights to explore and purchase mineral lands (e.g., section 2319 R.S.) do not authorize entry for prospecting on a duly established military reservation; mineral lands intended by statute are those included within 'public lands.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenge mineral entries on reservations as unauthorized trespass; verify whether land remains 'public land' under the statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Railroad rights of way and military reservations
rubrics_metrics.description: An act of Congress granting a railroad a right of way through 'the public lands' did not authorize entry and construction upon the soil of a military reservation, the reservation not being part of the 'public lands'; such entry is trespass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret grants of rights of way narrowly where reservations are involved; seek specific congressional authorization for incursions upon reservations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indian reservations not subject to military occupation
rubrics_metrics.description: Land set apart as part of an Indian reservation under treaty cannot be occupied as a military reserve, nor can a military post be maintained there in derogation of treaty terms or against the consent of the Interior Department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect treaty-created Indian reservations; coordinate with Interior and obtain necessary consents or legislation before locating military posts on such lands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectifying survey errors affecting reserved lands
rubrics_metrics.description: Where survey error locates a post on lands granted to the State as school land instead of reserved military land, the preferable mode of rectification is legislation of Congress granting the omitted section to the State and acceptance followed by state cession to the United States of exclusive jurisdiction over the actually occupied section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use legislative remedies to correct boundary/survey errors implicating state grants and federal reservations; coordinate with state legislatures for cession of jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer and re-control of reservations under statute
rubrics_metrics.description: Lands once duly reserved become separated from public lands; the President cannot restore them to original status absent statutory authority, though under the act of July 5, 1884 he may place 'useless' reservations under Interior for disposition, and the practice allows revocation of orders placing lands under Interior control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow statutory channels for transfer or sale of reservations; be mindful that transfer may be revocable and that special statutory provisions govern disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of abandoned military reservations in territories
rubrics_metrics.description: Where land laws are not applicable (e.g., Philippine Islands), abandoned military reservations revert to the control of the local governing commission (e.g., Philippines Commission).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider local statutory frameworks for disposition of abandoned reservations in territories and possessions; consult enabling acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tideland rights and military authority limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Ownership and jurisdiction of soil between high and low water mark on navigable waters within or bordering a State are vested in the State; military authorities cannot legally prevent exercise of common fisheries rights below high-water mark except as State law abridges them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid extending military control below high-water mark where State tidelands and common fisheries rights prevail; coordinate with State authorities when needs affect tidelands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tidelands in Territories belong to US sovereign
rubrics_metrics.description: In a Territory the sovereign right to the whole soil is exclusively in the United States; reservation of an island in tidewaters of a Territory includes its soil down to high-water mark and all its tidelands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between State and Territory contexts when assessing ownership of tidelands; assert federal ownership in Territories unless otherwise provided by Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expulsion and treatment of squatters and trespassers
rubrics_metrics.description: Squatters and other trespassers may and should be expelled, by military force if necessary, from a military reservation; they should be allowed reasonable time to remove their property, and material abandoned may be utilized by the commander for public works; squatters may also be removed by criminal proceedings or civil action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide reasonable notice prior to forcible eviction; document improvements and abandonment; use criminal or civil remedies where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards for improvements by squatters may be binding
rubrics_metrics.description: Where squatters have made considerable improvements and their value has been duly estimated by a board constituted by the department commander, an award by the Secretary of War, acquiesced in by the claimant, may be sued upon in the Court of Claims, which will accept such award as conclusive in absence of fraud or mistake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use properly constituted boards to estimate improvement value and make awards; expect courts to respect such awards absent evidence of fraud or mistake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminality of cutting timber or removing grass on reservations
rubrics_metrics.description: The cutting of timber on a military reservation is an offense against the United States (section 5388 R.S. and related acts); grass cut and removed as hay constitutes larceny under applicable statutes, and persons committing such trespasses may be removed and prevented from carrying off government property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce penal statutes against unauthorized cutting/removal of timber and grass; commanders may use necessary force to prevent removal of government property and to eject trespassers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to remove injurious intrusions and requirement of notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The authority to remove trespassers, their structures and property from United States land embraced in a military reservation applies especially where the intrusion is injurious (e.g., a sewer intended to discharge into a federal sewer); reasonable notice should be given municipal authorities to remove their property before resorting to military force, and precautions should be taken to prevent harmful connections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide notice to municipal authorities and take interim precautions to protect federal systems before using force; document injurious impact and necessity for removal.
